title: Integrated bulk, single-nucleus, spatial transcriptomic, and proteomic analyses identify Crot-associated proximal-tubule peroxisomal dysregulation in murine renal ischemia-reperfusion injury
content:
by Yuan Yang, Yi Chen, Pin Lan, Kechun Zhou

Background

Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) underlies acute kidney injury after transplantation, shock, and major surgery. Proximal-tubule metabolic dysfunction shapes injury and repair. Peroxisomes shorten fatty acids and export products, but their cross-omic behavior in acute renal IRI remains unclear.

Methods

We integrated two murine bulk RNA-sequencing discovery cohorts and two validation cohorts. Dataset-adjusted differential expression, pathway analysis, and training-only feature selection defined peroxisome-associated candidates. Nested validation assessed selection and predictive performance separately. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing resolved cellular localization, animal-level pseudobulk, and pseudotime dynamics. Segment 3 proximal-tubule (PTS3) expression informed a metabolic model for in silico Crot knockout. Spatial, proteomic, and patient-level human analyses assessed tissue distribution and cross-layer support.

Results

The discovery cohorts yielded 1,477 differentially expressed genes, with negative enrichment of peroxisome and fatty-acid programs. Crot decreased and Acot5 increased across external mouse cohorts. Nested L1 models retained Crot in 40/50 fits and Acot5 in none. Crot decreased within PTS3 at all IRI time points; its animal-aware pseudotime association was weaker and heterogeneous. Without exogenous octanoate, simulated Crot knockout reduced C8-carnitine output capacity by 18.2%−50.6%. Additional spatial cohorts supported lower whole-section Crot, with cohort-dependent proximal-tubule-rich results. Proteomics showed lower acute CROT abundance, replicated in an independent cohort with three mice per group (3 d, FDR = 0.006). Human GSE210622 showed lower proximal-tubule CROT, with sensitivity to control source; three other human contexts did not reproduce this decrease, indicating limited cross-cohort consistency.

Conclusions

Acute murine renal IRI is accompanied by suppression of proximal-tubule peroxisomal lipid-handling programs. Convergent bulk, single-nucleus, metabolic-modeling, spatial, and protein evidence prioritizes Crot for mechanistic investigation.
